## Active

### D-269 — The demo logs in against blong-access-mock, with srv for the ports

> _2026-09-25 · demo/handler-test-poc · active_

The demo logs in through `blong-access-mock`. That was the user's call between the three options,
and it works: the suite now passes 51 of 51 subtests, where before this session every scenario
stopped at the login.

Three pieces were needed together, and none of them alone was enough. First, `srv` (blong-server) in
the server config: the login calls the access realm over `/rpc/ports/access/request`, and that route
is served by the subject dispatch blong-server contributes, not by the realm that owns the
namespace. Without it the call 404s even with the mock loaded, which is what made the
missing-access-realm diagnosis look right for so long. Second, `access` set to
`blong-access-mock/server.ts`, whose `access.credential.check` answers from a constant — the real
access realm would also work but brings blong-core and a database. Third, `login.login.methods` with
`sessionCreate`, `auditRecord` and `sessionCleanup` false, so the token is stateless and nothing
touches a session table.

On top of the wiring, each scenario opens with a login step and every authenticated step awaits it.
That ordering is not optional: the bearer token is what the login response delivered, so a call sent
before the response lands goes out without it.

Two deliberate departures from the obvious route are worth keeping in mind. The scenarios call
`loginTokenCreate` directly instead of the codec realm's `testLoginTokenCreate` helper, because the
helper resolves that call inside the codec namespace's own port, where this suite has nothing to
reach. And the demo no longer imports `codec.test` into its test dispatch, since the helper was the
only thing it was there for.

## Superseded

### D-268 — Route (a) half landed, the scenarios left on the helper

> _2026-09-25 · demo/handler-test-poc · superseded_

order/testDispatch.ts now imports login.login (the group the login realm's own port imports),
because without it no login request is sent at all: verified by tracing that
loginTokenCreateRequestSend fires and the server answers a real status, where before the adapter
only ever saw order.order.create.

The scenarios themselves were left on testLoginTokenCreate: switching them to the ordered direct
login is what option 1 asks for and it dispatches correctly, but it also hangs on the failed login
the missing access realm produces, so the switch belongs in the same change as that realm, not
before it. Both halves and the evidence are in T-149.

Superseded: the scenarios were switched to their own login step in the same change that added
blong-access-mock and srv, exactly as this entry said they should be.
